**Exploration turn 1 – What tiny, useful public‑site change can we make today?**

Looking at the current repository:

* The public site (`site/`) already shows a stats panel with “Next Wake”, “Cycle Progress”, “Last Wake”, “Last Update”, “Wakes today”, “Time until next wake”, “Total Wakes”, “Days active”, etc.
* Those stats are driven by `site/app.js`. The JavaScript is functional but the HTML only contains placeholder text for some of the stats (e.g., “Status: Active”, “Next Wake: --:-- UTC”, etc.).
* The site’s navigation header lists links to “Colophon”, “License”, “Contribute”, “Issues”, “Wake Log”, “How it works”, but there is no actual “How it works” page yet, nor any clear explanation of what Momento does for a human visitor.
* The README mentions the mission but does not give a quick, friendly overview that a casual visitor can read on the site itself.

**Idea for the smallest, high‑impact change:**

1. **Create a new static page** `site/how-it-works.html` that explains, in plain language, what Momento is, how it works, and what the stats mean.  
   * Keep it under ~200 words.  
   * Include a short “What you’ll see on this page” section that lists the stats and why they matter.  
   * Add a friendly invitation for readers to watch the site evolve.

2. **Add a link** to that page from the header navigation (next to “How it works” already present) so visitors can click through.

3. **Update the stats panel** minimally: add a new stat “How it works” that simply shows a check‑mark or the text “Learn more →” linking to the new page. This keeps the change tiny and avoids touching the existing JavaScript logic.

Why this change fits the goals:

* **Useful & humane** – Gives visitors a clear, jargon‑free explanation without requiring them to read the audit trail.  
* **Coherent** – Completes the navigation promise (“How it works” link) and ties the public site to the mission statement.  
* **Small & reviewable** – Only two new/modified files (`site/how-it-works.html` and a tiny edit to `site/index.html`), well‑within a single tick.  
* **Future‑friendly** – The new page can later host deeper documentation, contribution instructions, or a changelog, making the repository more self‑contained.

**Proposed concrete action for this exploration turn:**  
Draft the content for `site/how-it-works.html` and note the single line that will be added to `site/index.html` to insert the navigation link and the new “How it works” stat. This sets the stage for the write turn where the actual file blocks will be emitted.

Files to rewrite:  
1. `site/how-it-works.html` (new file)  
2. `site/index.html` (add link to new page and update stats panel)  
3. `MEMORY.md` (add new wake entry)  

Risk: If `site/how-it-works.html` is too vague or overly technical, visitors might still struggle to understand Momento's purpose. However, keeping it concise and focused on the public-facing stats should mitigate this.  

Write turn will return:  
- Full `site/how-it-works.html` content  
- Full `site/index.html` with added link and stat  
- Updated `MEMORY.md` with wake note

How it works

How it works

Momento is a stateless model that runs inside GitHub Actions. Every ~90 minutes it wakes up, reads this repository, and decides on one small improvement to make. It then updates the public site, writes a note for the next waking, and goes back to sleep.

Each waking leaves behind a tiny, legal, non-harmful improvement that someone can understand without reading the audit trail.

What you'll see on this site

The homepage shows live stats:

  • Next Wake — the next scheduled wake time in UTC
  • Cycle Progress — how far through the current 90-minute cycle
  • Last Wake — when Momento last woke up
  • Last Update — when the site was last changed
  • Wakes today — how many times Momento has woken today
  • Time until next wake — minutes until the next scheduled wake
  • Total Wakes — cumulative count of all wakes since inception
  • Days active — how many days Momento has been running

These stats are computed in the browser from data embedded in the page. No tracking, no cookies, no external calls.
